newsitem.title: EGYPT: Three killed in Egypt at protest over farm law.
newsitem.headline: Three killed in Egypt at protest over farm law.

text.p: Three people were killed and dozens hurt in southern Egypt on Tuesday when police broke up a riot by farmers to protest a new farm land law, the interior ministry and security sources said.

The ministry said in a statement that farm tenants in the villages of Qulusna and Kawadi, in Minya province, had fired arms, threw stones at cars and broke the windows of the farm cooperative society.
It said three people, including a 70-year-old man and a teenaged boy, were killed "when security forces trid to control the situation".

Security sources said that police arrested dozens of the farm tenant demonstrators who also set fire to pieces of wood on the main road that links the southern provinces, blocking car and train traffic for about four hours.
The demonstrators also set fire to the house of one of the main landlords in the area and a public-transport bus, they said.
The sources said dozens of people were hurt in the riots. Police have slapped a curfew on the two villages, they added.
"The situation is now under control," the interior ministry statement said.
The detained farmers could face charges of causing public trouble, organising a demonstration and wasting public money. Demonstrations are illegal in Egypt.

The new law will come into effect in October and end the perpetuated relationship between landlords and tenants, but the sources said cooperative societies had already received instructions to start procedures for moving possession documents from tenants to land-owners.
The law, and other recently introduced bills, scrap many provisions installed by the late socialist president Gamal Abdel-Nasser in the late 1950s.
The law as it stands makes it almost impossible for land-owners to sell their land without splitting the price with tenants.
Last month, police arrested 26 farmers for allegedly demonstrating in another southern province, where protesters burnt down two government buildings to protest at the law.
